takeaway: Physiological dead space includes alveolar dead space: ventilated alveoli with poor blood flow. Hypotension increases it; standing and bronchodilation raise anatomical dead space.

question.text: Which of the following increases the physiological dead space in the respiratory system?
question.say: Which of the following increases the physiological dead space in the respiratory system?

lines.text: Dead space is air that reaches the lungs but does not take part in gas exchange.
Anatomical dead space is the air-conveying ducts, and it grows when you stand or when the airways dilate.
Physiological dead space is bigger: it adds the alveoli that are ventilated but not perfused.
With hypotension, blood flow falls, so the alveoli hold air but get no blood.
Air but no blood: the tap is closed, so alveolar dead space grows.
Emphysema, pulmonary embolism and positive pressure ventilation do the same, so hypotension is the answer.
